Furthermore, in order to broaden the isolated frequency band, the impedance Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">iso</sub> with the series connected resistor and capacitor on the right side of the middle coupled line is adopted. This power divider is fabricated on the substrate Rogers RO4003C, with a compact size of 15.19 mm × 11.4 mm.

articleTitle: An all-digital on-chip clock generator using relative reference modeling
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: An all-digital on-chip clock generator is proposed in this paper. It features the tolerance of process, voltage and temperature variation according to the special algorithm. The clock generator depends on CMOS standard delay cell without any external clock source, and the periods of CMOS standard delay cell are calculated by the linear polynomial fitting. The proposed on-chip clock generator has been implemented in 180 nm CMOS. The output clock is 10MHz~40MHz adjustable, and tolerates the process, voltage and temperature variation. The frequency error is less than 2.9% with 1.6V-1.8V supply voltage and 0°C-80°C temperature variation. The phase noise is -116.44 dBc/Hz @ 25 MHz offset.

articleTitle: Broadband radio-frequency integrated circuits and modules for astronomical instruments in Taiwan
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Various kinds of broadband radio frequency integrated circuits for astronomical instrument were developed in Taiwan during past 18 years. In this paper the key technology and results, including the circuit design, testing, packaging and system integration are described.

articleTitle: Design of oscillator with band-pass quadrature outputs
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: An oscillator with band-pass quadrature outputs is proposed in this paper. Band-pass quadrature couplers are incorporated in the feedback path of the oscillator to improve stopband inhibition. The proposed oscillator was fabricated on an FR-4 substrate for verification. The measured output power at 2.06 GHz is -4.6 dBm. Phase noises of -104.8 dBc/Hz and -124.6 dBc/Hz at 100 kHz and 1 MHz offset frequencies are measured, respectively.

articleTitle: Design considerations and approaches for sensor interface circuits in smart sensor microsystems
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: With the future filled with a trillion sensors on the way, there is a large variety in the forms of smart sensor microsystems for different applications existing or emerging. The applications of smart sensor microsystems and corresponding use scenarios define important design requirements of sensor interface circuits such as physical parameters to sense, minimum detection limit, bandwidth, dynamic range, and sensing duty cycle. In this paper, we investigate how these application-dependent requirements lead to different design approaches for the sensor interface circuit, which is one of most essential parts in the smart sensor microsystem.

articleTitle: Highly linear SOI LDMOS power amplifier with combinated cascode structure
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A fully on-chip SOI LDMOS linear PA for WLAN is implemented in a SOI LDMOS process. A cascode of SOI CMOS and SOI LDMOS is used to overcome the breakdown issue of the SOI CMOS transistor. An adaptive power cell (APC) and specially designed CG bias network are adopted to achieve linear performance. This proposed PA has gain of 24.3 dB and output power of 20.2 dBm for an 802.11n modulated signal with the EVM of −25dB.

articleTitle: A stent based in-vivo bio-sensing system for glucose monitoring
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a stent based in-vivo bio-sensing system for glucose monitoring is introduced. Conventional glucose monitoring methods suffer from pain, inconvenience, and financial consumption. In order to overcome the problems, the method that the monitoring system is inserted into blood vessel and detecting the glucose level wirelessly is proposed in this paper. The system includes several blocks such as a sensor interface circuit, a communication block, a wireless power transfer block, and an antenna block. To implement the communication block, a delay locked loop (DLL) for an oscillator is designed and experimented. Also, to implement the wireless power transfer, rectifier and regulator are designed.

articleTitle: Design of the compact crossover with the cross-slotted lines
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A compact planar crossover with two intersecting channels is proposed. This crossover is constructed by a patch resonator and two cross-slotted lines. Moreover, the longer the cross slotted lines are, the smaller the proposed planar crossover is. In order to simplify the analysis of the proposed planar crossover, the approximate two-port equivalent circuit is provided. The measured performances match well with the theoretical results, which validates the proposed circuit.

articleTitle: EMG-signal regeneration and motor function rebuilding of paralyzed/anergic limbs based on communication principles and with RF-wireless technology
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This work presents motor function rebuilding of paralyzed limbs of hemiplegic patients after stroke and anergic limbs of senile people. The biomedical methods and the traditional physical methods for rehabilitation of the paralyses are reviewed. The core part is to discuss EMG-signal regeneration and the limb function rebuilding based on communication principles and functional electrical stimulation-a novel concept developed by the speakers. For the EMG-signal transmission, different radio-frequency (RF) transmission systems are utilized. The construction of the whole bio-electronic system and the preliminary experiments on healthy patients are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Report of clinical results in intraoperative wireless recording
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this work, clinical results of a wireless recording system for intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring during a spine correction surgery are reported. The wireless modules connecting directly to the subdermal needle electrodes transmit the waveforms detected in certain muscle areas to a computer via telemetry for real-time display, analysis and storage. Sufficient gain, bandwidth and digitalization preserve the integrity of the neural signal waveforms throughout the surgery. The feasibility of using wireless communication to quantitatively document the health of patient's neural system during spine manipulation is demonstrated. The waveforms are recorded in real time with high accuracy to assess the risks of injury. This demonstration validates the potentials for wireless signal acquisition in clinical settings and can enable more applications for precise diagnosis with benefits of elimination cluttered wires and electromagnetic interferences.

articleTitle: Compat wireless energy harvesting rectenna and measurement configuration with multiple continuous-wave transmitters
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A compact rectenna suitable for the tracking harmonic radar dedicated for small-sized creatures is designed and implemented. To efficiently harvest the RF power and radiate the doubled harmonic frequency for the tag of the harmonic radar system, the dualband 4-/8-GHz antenna is designed and implemented. The average gains at the two bands are -1.03 dBi and -2.37 dBi, respectively. Moreover, a two-stage Dickson rectifier at 4 GHz of a compact size 8.5×8.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> has the dc output voltage larger than 1 V as the input RF power higher than -5.5 dBm. The rectenna featuring a miniaturized size of 18×17 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> has been examined by a test system equipped with 3 identical CW transmitters.

articleTitle: A V-band beamforming transmitter front-end with full 360° phase shifting range
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a V-band transmitter frontend for beamforming phased array system. The front-end consists of a reflective-type phase shifter, a gain amplifier, a differential phase inverter, and a driver amplifier. The measured phase tuning range covers the full 360° range, from 55 to 65 GHz. The power gain is 9.5 dB, and the output P1dB is 4.7 dBm at 60 GHz. The chip size is 0.89 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in 90-nm CMOS.

articleTitle: A 0.3mW 1Mb/s high security proximity UWB transmitter with frequency/time-domain scrambling
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper describes an ultra-wideband (UWB) transmitter architecture for secure proximity communication. The transmitter achieves high security by utilizing a pseudorandom scrambling method for both frequency hopping in frequency domain and pulse position modulation (PPM) in time domain. In addition, the low transmitted power of -70dBm/MHz not only makes it difficult for other receivers to detect the signal but also makes the transmission worldwide compliant with existing wireless standards. A prototype 3-4GHz proximity transmitter is implemented in 0.18μm CMOS. The transmitter achieves 1Mb/s data rate with 0.3mW power from a 1.8V supply.

articleTitle: System-level evaluation of 300GHz CMOS wireless transmitter using cubic mixer
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A QAM-capable 300GHz CMOS transmitter operating above/max was recently reported. A key component is a cubic mixer, which is a tripler-based up-conversion mixer. This paper studies the SNR characteristics of cubic mixer theoretically for realizing high-speed communication. The condition of avoiding the interference between the RF signal and spur component is clarified.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of an indoor positioning system on SDR platform
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design and implementation of a high precision Indoor Positioning System (IPS), with average accuracy within 0.5 meter and 90% of positioning errors smaller than 0.9m in three trial environments. The transmitter continuously transmitted periodic PN code and the multiple receivers at fixed locations performed signal acquisition, tracking, and position calculation. Several techniques were also integrated to combat the severe multipath effect. Finally, a Software Defined Radio (SDR) platform with baseband processing implemented in FPGA was constructed for real-time demonstration and validation of the effectiveness of this proposed IPS solution.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit model of multi-layered coils for integrated sensor applications in medium-wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Representation of an accurate equivalent circuit model of sensor coil is an important issue, an operational frequency being higher. Generally, the coil is represented by an inductance element connected with a resistance in series and a capacitance in parallel. In use of multi-layered coils at medium wave frequencies, it is however considered that the correction of the model should be needed to make the accurate equivalent circuit model. Having this fact in minds, inductances, resistances, and capacitances of the multi-layered coils were extracted by the electromagnetic field simulator and a new type of equivalent circuit of the multilayered coil was evaluated by comparing the calculated results with the measured ones. And the validity was confirmed in this paper.

articleTitle: Electro-thermal-stress analysis of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs breakdown under intentional EMI
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper demonstrated electro-thermal-stress interaction of Gallium Nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) breakdown under intentional EMI. A series of GaN HEMT-based power amplifiers were designed and measured for their reliability. The crack area in the field plate of GaN HEMT was characterized experimentally. Electro-thermal-stress simulation was performed for capturing temperature and stress distributions over the structure so as to understand breakdown mechanism of GaN HEMTs.

articleTitle: Architectures of millimeter wave RF subsystems for 5G applications and their characteristics
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents the architectures of millimeter waves (mmW) RF subsystems under development by NTU and NCSIST joint team for the 5G applications. Based on the application scenario and link budget estimation, the specification of RF subsystem is defined, which has eight I/O ports to excite the antenna arrays. The concepts of beam switching links and multi-beam sector coverage are separately implemented to investigate their characteristics in the radio propagation. The target of system design aims to achieve 1GHz frequency bandwidth for 3∼5 Gbps data rate in a coverage area of 50m. Characteristics of RF components will be presented with a taped system demonstration in the conference presentation.

articleTitle: A 10–20 Gb/s CDR circuit with 6200ppm frequency tracking
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A 10-20 Gb/s clock and data recovery (CDR) circuit with frequency tracking is presented. Two digital phase interpolators (PIs) are used to track the frequency of input data. The loop bandwidth of the CDR circuit is adaptively adjusted. A mixed-mode PI is used to generate the recovered clock. This CDR circuit is fabricated in a 40 nm CMOS process and its area is 0.33×1.0 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Its power consumption is 97.2 mW with a supply voltage of 1.5 V. This CDR circuit can track the data with the down spread-spectrum clocking of 6200 ppm for a 20 Gb/s pseudo random binary sequence (PRBS) of 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>-1, when the bit-error rate is less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup>. The measured rms jitters of the retimed data are 2.78 ps and 2.33 ps for the data of 10 Gb/s and 20 Gb/s, respectively.

articleTitle: Terahertz systems made from nanotechnologies
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The infamous “Terahertz Gap” represents frequency spectrum that ranges from 0.3 to 3THz (or 300 to 3000GHz). It lies between traditional microwave and infrared domains but remains “untouchable” via either electronic or photonic means. The conventional “transit-time-limited” electronic devices can hardly operate even at its lowest frequency; the “band-gap-limited” photonic devices on the other hand can only operate beyond its highest frequency. Since wavelengths range from 1000 to 100 μm, Terahertz signals tend to behave quasi-optically and are potentially instrumental for a wide range of scientific and industrial applications. Those include high-data rate, short distance and secured wireless & wireline communications, telemetric and remote sensing based on high-resolution radar, spectrometer and imagers for intelligent traffic/landing control, safety/security screening and bio-medical/food/drug sensing, and analysis and controls. In this talk, we will discuss fundamental & technical challenges involved in building Terahertz systems-on-chip from nano-dimensional CMOS technologies and progress made recently at UCLA and NCTU to overcome electronic/photonic barriers for realizing highly integrated (sub)-mm-Wave and Terahertz systems.
